cases.purpose: Show that doas and sudo select their route from the production privcmd node name and never leave the versioned route once it is selected.
cases.oracle: The route rules stated in loadables/common/authority-route.h and docs/authority-routes.md: a consumer whose production node name is absent behaves as before the versioned protocol; a consumer whose node name exists in any form is committed to the versioned protocol and every failure is final. The stand-in names are made by the fixture in a private /dev and answer no authority ioctl, so no expectation depends on a working authority. Marker files written only by the delegate, the target or the session are the independent observation of what ran.
cases.comparison: For an absent name and four stand-in forms of the name (unrelated character device, regular file, dangling symbolic link, directory) a caller with uid 3001 runs doas, sudo and sudo -l with an external delegate configured. Absent: the delegate marker appears and no authority-v2 diagnostic is printed. Present: nonzero status, an authority-v2 diagnostic, and neither the delegate marker nor the target marker. A final row shows uid 0 keeping its direct route with the name present: the target marker is owned by uid 3001.
cases.script:
. /opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/authority-route-fixture.sh || exit 125
route_guard && route_private_dev && route_accounts || exit 125
: >"$HOME/route-stderr.log" || exit 125
printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/sh' ': > /tmp/parity-case/marks/delegate' >delegate || exit 125
printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/sh' ': > /tmp/parity-case/marks/target' >target || exit 125
/usr/bin/chmod 755 delegate target || exit 125
export BASHDOAS_EXTERNAL=$PWD/delegate BASHSUDO_EXTERNAL=$PWD/delegate
row() {
  local err rc
  route_clear
  err=$(route_as_alice "$2" 2>&1 >/dev/null </dev/null); rc=$?
  printf '%s: status=%s %s\n' "$1" "$rc" "$err" >>"$HOME/route-stderr.log"
  printf '%s refused=%s v2-diagnostic=%s delegate=%s target=%s\n' "$1" \
    "$([[ $rc != 0 ]] && echo yes || echo no)" "$([[ $err == *authority-v2:* ]] && echo yes || echo no)" \
    "$(route_mark delegate)" "$(route_mark target)"
}
for kind in absent chardev regular symlink dir; do
  route_node bashos-privcmd-v2 "$kind" || exit 125
  row "$kind doas" "doas -n $PWD/target"
  row "$kind sudo" "sudo -n $PWD/target"
  row "$kind sudo-list" "sudo -l"
done
route_node bashos-privcmd-v2 chardev || exit 125
route_clear
doas -u alice "$PWD/target" </dev/null; rc=$?
printf 'chardev doas-uid0 status=%s target=%s owner=%s\n' "$rc" "$(route_mark target)" "$(/usr/bin/stat -c %u marks/target 2>/dev/null)"
cases.stdout:
absent doas refused=no v2-diagnostic=no delegate=ran target=absent
absent sudo refused=no v2-diagnostic=no delegate=ran target=absent
absent sudo-list refused=no v2-diagnostic=no delegate=ran target=absent
chardev doas refused=yes v2-diagnostic=yes delegate=absent target=absent
chardev sudo refused=yes v2-diagnostic=yes delegate=absent target=absent
chardev sudo-list refused=yes v2-diagnostic=yes delegate=absent target=absent
regular doas refused=yes v2-diagnostic=yes delegate=absent target=absent
regular sudo refused=yes v2-diagnostic=yes delegate=absent target=absent
regular sudo-list refused=yes v2-diagnostic=yes delegate=absent target=absent
symlink doas refused=yes v2-diagnostic=yes delegate=absent target=absent
symlink sudo refused=yes v2-diagnostic=yes delegate=absent target=absent
symlink sudo-list refused=yes v2-diagnostic=yes delegate=absent target=absent
dir doas refused=yes v2-diagnostic=yes delegate=absent target=absent
dir sudo refused=yes v2-diagnostic=yes delegate=absent target=absent
dir sudo-list refused=yes v2-diagnostic=yes delegate=absent target=absent
chardev doas-uid0 status=0 target=ran owner=3001

cases.purpose: Show that login login and login become select their route from the production identity node name and fail closed once the versioned route is selected.
cases.oracle: The route rules stated in loadables/common/authority-route.h and docs/authority-routes.md: a consumer whose production node name is absent behaves as before the versioned protocol; a consumer whose node name exists in any form is committed to the versioned protocol and every failure is final. The stand-in names are made by the fixture in a private /dev and answer no authority ioctl, so no expectation depends on a working authority. Marker files written only by the delegate, the target or the session are the independent observation of what ran.
cases.comparison: For an absent name and four stand-in forms, uid 0 runs login become without a proof under BASHLOGIN_REQUIRE_KERNEL_TOKEN=0, with --auth-token, with --auth-fd on a descriptor that is not the authority, and login login on a non-terminal. Absent: the environment opt-out still produces a session marker, the token forms fail with the historical diagnostics, and login prints its prompt. Present: every form is refused with a versioned diagnostic, no session marker appears and no login prompt is printed.
cases.script:
. /opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/authority-route-fixture.sh || exit 125
route_guard && route_private_dev && route_accounts || exit 125
: >"$HOME/route-stderr.log" || exit 125
export BASHLOGIN_REQUIRE_KERNEL_TOKEN=0
token=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
become_plain() { login become alice -c ': > /tmp/parity-case/marks/session'; }
become_token() { login become alice --auth-token "$token" -c ': > /tmp/parity-case/marks/session'; }
become_fd() { login become alice --auth-fd 9 -c ': > /tmp/parity-case/marks/session' 9</dev/null; }
login_plain() { login login; }
row() {
  local label=$1 err rc; shift
  route_clear
  err=$("$@" 2>&1 >stdout.tmp </dev/null); rc=$?
  printf '%s: status=%s %s\n' "$label" "$rc" "$err" >>"$HOME/route-stderr.log"
  printf '%s refused=%s versioned-diagnostic=%s session=%s prompt=%s\n' "$label" \
    "$([[ $rc != 0 ]] && echo yes || echo no)" \
    "$([[ $err == *versioned* || $err == *login-v2:* ]] && echo yes || echo no)" \
    "$(route_mark session)" "$([[ $(<stdout.tmp) == *' login: '* ]] && echo yes || echo no)"
}
for kind in absent chardev regular symlink dir; do
  route_node bashos-auth-v2 "$kind" || exit 125
  row "$kind become" become_plain
  row "$kind become-token" become_token
  row "$kind become-fd" become_fd
  row "$kind login" login_plain
done

absent become-fd refused=yes versioned-diagnostic=no session=absent prompt=no

cases.purpose: Show that su and the descriptor-explicit auth verbs select their route from the production node names and fail closed once the versioned route is selected.
cases.oracle: The route rules stated in loadables/common/authority-route.h and docs/authority-routes.md: a consumer whose production node name is absent behaves as before the versioned protocol; a consumer whose node name exists in any form is committed to the versioned protocol and every failure is final. The stand-in names are made by the fixture in a private /dev and answer no authority ioctl, so no expectation depends on a working authority. Marker files written only by the delegate, the target or the session are the independent observation of what ran.
cases.comparison: For an absent name and four stand-in forms of each node, su runs as uid 0 and as uid 3001, auth verify-login runs on a descriptor that is not the authority, and auth privcmd-probe, privcmd-authz and audit-read run as uid 0. Every row must be refused with no effect marker and no bound output variable; rows with the name present must carry a versioned-authority diagnostic and rows with the name absent must not, which distinguishes the committed route from the historical refusal.
cases.script:
. /opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/authority-route-fixture.sh || exit 125
route_guard && route_private_dev && route_accounts || exit 125
: >"$HOME/route-stderr.log" || exit 125
phc='$argon2id$v=19$m=1024,t=1,p=1$c29tZXNhbHQ$CTFhFdXPJO1aFaMaO6Mm5c8y7cJHAph8ArZWb2GRPPc'
su_root() { su --no-login -c ': > /tmp/parity-case/marks/effect' alice; }
su_alice() { route_as_alice "su --no-login -c ': > /tmp/parity-case/marks/effect' alice"; }
auth_verify() {
  local TOK=unset rc
  auth verify-login 9 1 alice "$phc" TOK 9<>/dev/null; rc=$?
  [[ $TOK == unset ]] || : > marks/effect
  return "$rc"
}
auth_probe() { auth privcmd-probe && : > marks/effect; }
auth_authz() { auth privcmd-authz 9 exec 0 0 -- /bin/true 9<>/dev/null && : > marks/effect; }
auth_audit() { auth audit-read 9 9<>/dev/null && : > marks/effect; }
row() {
  local label=$1 err rc; shift
  route_clear
  err=$("$@" 2>&1 >/dev/null </dev/null); rc=$?
  printf '%s: status=%s %s\n' "$label" "$rc" "$err" >>"$HOME/route-stderr.log"
  printf '%s refused=%s versioned-diagnostic=%s effect=%s\n' "$label" \
    "$([[ $rc != 0 ]] && echo yes || echo no)" \
    "$([[ $err == *'versioned authority'* || $err == *bashos-privcmd-v2* ]] && echo yes || echo no)" \
    "$(route_mark effect)"
}
for kind in absent chardev regular symlink dir; do
  route_node bashos-auth-v2 "$kind" || exit 125
  row "identity $kind su-uid0" su_root
  row "identity $kind su-user" su_alice
  row "identity $kind auth-verify-login" auth_verify
done
route_node bashos-auth-v2 absent || exit 125
for kind in absent chardev regular symlink dir; do
  route_node bashos-privcmd-v2 "$kind" || exit 125
  row "privcmd $kind auth-privcmd-probe" auth_probe
  row "privcmd $kind auth-privcmd-authz" auth_authz
  row "privcmd $kind auth-audit-read" auth_audit
done
